A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PercHead, with matching authors, core architecture, reconstruction tasks, and editing framework. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction results on Ava-256 and NeRSemble, quantitative ablations, video reconstructions, and image- and text-conditioned editing examples.

after.justification: v2 reports original reconstruction and editing experiments, revised quantitative results, and additional loss diagnostics, robustness tests, and lightweight-model evaluations.

M1.justification: The core reconstruction and editing pipelines remain. Sharpening supervision changes from DINOv2, L1, and LPIPS in v1 Section 3.4 to only the DINOv2 layer-8 class token in v2 Section 3.3. Appendix C.6 also introduces four-layer lightweight variants; the expanded CNN and Gaussian descriptions alone do not establish architectural changes.

E1.justification: The Ava-256, NeRSemble, and VFHQ evaluation coverage is retained. v2 Appendix C.5 substantially broadens tested input conditions through held-out FFHQ images, UFDD examples, and SORA-generated inputs, including cartoons, unusual accessories, and difficult illumination.

E2.justification: v2 adds SphereHead to the Ava-256 and NeRSemble reconstruction comparisons, FaceLift to an additional Ava-256 comparison, and NeRFFaceEditing to geometric-editing comparisons. The original LGM, PanoHead, GAGAvatar, and LAM comparators remain.

E3.justification: The benchmark identities, cropping, and view tasks remain matched, but v1's shared pretrained CNN ablation control is replaced by a separately trained CNN for the LPIPS+L1 model. Reported CNN/editing training durations change from 24/30 hours to 10/48 hours. New protocols examine epochs 1–3, token supervision after one epoch, and four-layer model configurations; SSIM is also omitted from the main ablation table.

E4.justification: v2 adds early-training comparisons across DINOv2 layers, patch-versus-class-token ablations, difficult-input tests of the loss and sharpening module, and lightweight-model cost/quality analyses. It also examines localized versus large geometric edits. Existing data/loss ablations remain, although the quantitative LPIPS+L1-without-CNN comparison is removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. The additional experiments retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: Primary reconstruction and ablation values change beyond rounding. For example, Ava-256 novel-view PSNR changes from 16.08 to 16.4 while LPIPS changes from 0.2666 to 0.269 for the revised model. Under the changed CNN controls, LPIPS+L1 now beats the full model on ablation LPIPS, reversing v1's ordering. New comparator, robustness, early-training, and lightweight-model results substantially expand the evidence.

T1.justification: v2 explicitly defines tanh-bounded FLAME-relative Gaussian positions in Equation 3 and a multiplicative perceptual-loss combination in Equation 7, details left unspecified in v1. These are limited mathematical additions; the decoder recurrence is retained, and no theorems or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The principal claims of strong novel/extreme-view reconstruction and disentangled editing remain. v2's abstract adds an explicit claim that the perceptual loss is a drop-in replacement for standard losses, and its contributions emphasize supervision solely through deep perceptual features.

C2.justification: v2 qualifies v1's temporal-coherence discussion by acknowledging flickering and adds CLIP-related identity limitations, localized-editing tradeoffs, and failures involving unusual glasses or unrealistic faces. It introduces substantive interpretations of layer/token supervision and complementary loss behavior. The earlier blanket limitation concerning non-real-time inference is removed.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents AdamW settings, epoch counts, architecture dimensions and attention heads, the 3,000-image FFHQ subset, view/occlusion filtering, and sharpening-module processing. It adds component timing and memory measurements and explicitly states that training code, inference code, and the GUI are available through the project website. Newly disclosed settings do not establish that those settings changed.

R1.justification: v2 expands discussion and citations for SphereHead, FaceLift, Avat3r, inversion/diffusion approaches, and perceptual representations, while dropping the GRM and Feng et al. (2021) references. The existing positioning relative to GAN/NeRF pipelines and conventional supervision remains broadly intact.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method exposition, and experimental discussion are extensively rewritten. Separate encoder, decoder, and rendering subsections are consolidated, training receives its own subsection, and the supplement is reorganized into thematic sections A–G, retaining earlier processing and visualization material within that structure.

P2.justification: Figures 1 and 2 are substantially redrawn, comparison figures gain methods and examples, and the ablation display is redesigned. Reconstruction tables are reorganized by dataset, with NeRSemble moved to the supplement. Numerous new loss-analysis, robustness, editing, and computational-cost displays materially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens experimental support and reproducibility through relevant new comparators, a separately trained LPIPS+L1 control, targeted loss diagnostics, robustness tests, and detailed training specifications. Its more explicit temporal and editing limitations also improve claim calibration. These gains address important weaknesses in v1 and outweigh local reporting problems, including Table 5's SSIM heading above values around 15–16.
